research_question: When multilingual tool-use performance changes, when is the load-bearing cause semantic action selection and when is it the language/interface/evaluator contract through which the action is expressed and scored?
decision_owner: Agent benchmark and tool-interface designers deciding whether to change the model, interface contract, or evaluation interpretation.
worlds: W1: Language changes the selected action or intended arguments.
W2: The intended action is intact, but language-bearing parameter values violate a rigid execution interface.
W3: Translation, prompt templates, dataset filtering, or judging metrics create the apparent capability gap.
discriminator: A revision-pinned factorial comparison holding task intent and tool semantics fixed while varying query, schema, parameter-value, and evaluator languages, with executable outcomes and independent semantic adjudication.
falsifier: The apparent language effect disappears under interface-normalized execution and independent semantic scoring, or is fully explained by translation/template artifacts.
scope: Method-free R0 problem framing; any benchmark, replay system, or visualization is an instrument.
does_not_establish: Review-only source reduction; no gap, novelty, prevalence, proposal, or lifecycle transition is established.

source_spans.title: Lost in Execution: On the Multilingual Robustness of Tool Calling in Large Language Models
source_spans.observation: Separates correct semantic intent from non-executable language-interface values under controlled single-turn calls.
source_spans.resolves: Supplies a concrete interface-failure world and its limits.
source_spans.leaves_unresolved: Whether the distinction transports to long-horizon workflows or broad languages.
source_spans.does_not_establish: Long-horizon behavior, all languages, real deployment incidence, or the superiority of one interface design.

source_spans.title: MASSIVE-Agents: A Benchmark for Multilingual Function-Calling in 52 Languages
source_spans.observation: Shows broad multilingual variation under a particular parallel-data and scoring contract.
source_spans.resolves: Supplies coverage and a competing benchmark-level observation.
source_spans.leaves_unresolved: Which causal layer produces the observed gaps.
source_spans.does_not_establish: That performance gaps are caused specifically by semantic action selection rather than translation, interface, data, or evaluator contracts.

derived_questions.question: Which language-bearing surface first changes the executable action trace?
derived_questions.smallest_discriminator: One frozen task crossed across query, schema, parameter-value, and evaluator languages.

derived_questions.question: Does semantic-equivalent scoring reverse model or language rankings relative to strict AST scoring?
derived_questions.smallest_discriminator: A blinded paired adjudication on the same model outputs.
